name: C# Shellcode Runner & Process Injection
description: A compiled runner keeps the malicious bytes out of any script AMSI can inspect. Self-injection allocates RWX in the current process (VirtualAlloc), copies the shellcode, and runs it with CreateThread. Remote injection targets a trusted signed process (OpenProcess explorer.exe, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread) so the callback comes from a legitimate binary, defeating simple process heuristics.

notes: Compile the C# runner on Kali with mcs runner.cs -out:runner.exe, or cross-compile with mono. For remote injection, pick a stable signed process (explorer, svchost, notepad) that matches your shellcode arch (x64). Add the P-Invoke signatures via DllImport (kernel32.dll): VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread, OpenProcess. Because the shellcode only lives in the target process memory, on-disk AV never scans it — but behavioral engines flag VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread in sequence, so obfuscate the API call chain or use indirect syscalls for hardened targets. Pair with amsi-bypass if delivering via PowerShell first.

recommended.note: Kill AMSI before any PowerShell stage that loads or drops the runner.

defense.why_it_works: Process injection allocates memory in a remote process (OpenProcess → VirtualAllocEx), writes shellcode into it (WriteProcessMemory), and starts a remote thread to execute it (CreateRemoteThread or NtCreateThreadEx). The shellcode runs inside the target process's address space — EDR sees network/behavior anomalies from the target process (e.g., explorer.exe making C2 connections), not from the injecting process.
defense.prerequisites: Local admin or SeDebugPrivilege (for injecting into processes owned by other users). Target process PID. C# or C++ for the injector. Shellcode payload. AMSI bypass if injecting from PowerShell.
defense.impact: T1055 Process Injection + T1620 Reflective Code Loading. Executes shellcode under the identity and security context of the target process, hiding C2 communication within a trusted process. Evades process-level detection by attributing behavior to a legitimate process.
defense.detection:
Sysmon Event 8: CreateRemoteThread in non-related processes. EDR: VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread API sequence from a process that doesn't normally perform injection. Memory scan: shellcode in the target process's memory. Defender for Endpoint: 'Remote process injection' behavioral alert. ETW: kernel-level thread creation events.
Process injection by correlating memory manipulation API calls (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory), suspicious thread creation (CreateRemoteThread), and unusual DLL loads within another process's context (DET0508/AN1399).
ptrace- or memfd-based injection through audit logs capturing system calls (ptrace, mmap) targeting running processes along with suspicious file descriptors or memory writes (AN1400).
Memory-based injection via task_for_pid, mach_vm_write, and dylib injection patterns through DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or manual memory mapping on macOS (AN1401).
defense.artifacts: Sysmon Event 8: CreateRemoteThread from injecting process to target | EDR alert: process injection API sequence | Memory scan: injected code in target process | Sysmon Event 10: source process opening handle to target (OpenProcess) | Anomalous network connection from target process
defense.prevention:
EDR with injection detection. WDAC with memory integrity: Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI) prevents injection into protected processes. Protected Process Light (PPL) for critical processes. Block injection into high-value processes (lsass.exe, csrss.exe) via PPL. Deploy Defender for Endpoint P2 (advanced injection detection).
Behavior Prevention on Endpoint: Configure endpoint security solutions to block process injection based on common injection sequences; Windows 10 ASR rules can prevent Office applications from code injection.
Privileged Account Management: Use Yama (ptrace_scope) on Linux to restrict ptrace to privileged users; deploy security kernel modules.
defense.evasion: Use indirect syscalls (NtCreateThreadEx directly) to bypass API-level hooks. Inject into processes owned by current user (no SeDebug required). Use less-detected injection techniques: APC injection, Atom Bombing, reflective DLL injection. Use a signed loader process.
defense.misconfiguration: No EDR with memory injection detection. HVCI not enabled. No Sysmon Event 8 rule. PPL not configured for critical processes.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# No Sysmon Event 8 configured:
# sysmon -accepteula -i (no config) → missing CreateRemoteThread monitoring

# HVCI not enabled:
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\DeviceGuard').HypervisorEnforcedCodeIntegrity  # 0
# → Unsigned code injectable into any non-PPL process
defense.secure_config:
# Enable Sysmon with CreateRemoteThread monitoring:
# sysmon config:
# <CreateRemoteThread onmatch='include'>
#   <TargetImage condition='is not'>C:\Windows\system32\svchost.exe</TargetImage>
# </CreateRemoteThread>

# Enable HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity):
# Computer Config → Admin Templates → System → Device Guard
# → Turn on Virtualization Based Security: Enabled
# → Code Integrity Policy: HVCI Enabled
